subject: Post-demo: reliability validation plan & next tests against CloudCore APIs
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Shah <sanjay@cloudcore.com>, Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@cloudcore.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-14T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: reliability validation plan & next tests against CloudCore APIs

Hi Sanjay / Alicia,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great discussion and really helpful context about the production SLAs you need for the personalization / search use case. As promised, I wanted to capture proposed next steps so we can move the evaluation from demo → hands-on validation. Summary below: 

1) Objectives
- Confirm steady-state uptime behavior under realistic traffic patterns (95/99/99.9 SLO targets)
- Compare error profiles and throttling under burst traffic vs CloudCore's hosted inference API
- Measure tail latency and cold-start behaviors for concurrent sessions (50/100/500 users)

2) Proposed tests (see attached redwood-test-plan-v1.xlsx)
- Latency bakeoff (p95/p99/p999) across sequence lengths and batch sizes
- Error-injection runs to evaluate automatic failover to model variants and retry behavior
- Rate-limit threshold sweeps to map soft/hard throttling and 429 behavior

3) Owners & timing
- Redwood: Marcus to run the server-side workload scripts and provide detailed logs + KV cache traces
- CloudCore: Sanjay to provide the representative traffic shape and any rate-limit / regional constraints we should mimic
- Target window: next week (Mon–Wed) for controlled runs, Thurs for shared results review

4) Logistics / telemetry we need from you
- Exact API keys and any IP allow-listing windows (short-lived tokens are fine)
- Expected per-minute token volume and peak concurrent sessions

Marcus and Rafael — can you review the attached plan and call out any gaps (especially around failover instrumentation and KV cache visibility)?

Sanjay / Alicia — are you available Tues 8/18 10:00 PT for a 30-min alignment call to confirm the traffic profiles and to open the IP window? If that time doesn't work we can do Wed morning.

Thanks,

Tessa Morgan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
(t) 415-555-0186 | tessa.morgan@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood-test-plan-v1.xlsx (workbook: test matrix, scripts, expected outputs)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Sanjay Shah <sanjay@cloudcore.com>, Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@cloudcore.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-15T10:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: reliability validation plan & next tests against CloudCore APIs

Thanks Tessa — quick technical notes after reviewing the plan and the model shapes you shared in the call: 

- KV cache visibility: we'll emit per-request KV cache hit/miss counts and the cumulative cache size metric. That will help explain tail-latency differences when sequences reuse prefixes.

- Failover semantics: Redwood's routing supports model-variant fallback (quantized variant) and region fallback separately. For the experiment, I propose three scenarios: (A) normal routing to primary model, (B) induced GPU OOM on primary to force variant fallback, (C) simulated region outage (we'll route to an alternate region). We'll capture error codes and timestamps so you can reproduce mapping to your error budget policies.

- Rate limits: Redwood returns structured 429 with an RFC-compliant Retry-After header for soft limits. For hard per-account quotas we'll see 403+quota metadata. In the test plan I added a sweep that steps RPS from baseline → 5x baseline in 30% increments to map the soft-throttle curve.

- Measurement hooks: I attached a small bash/python harness in the plan sheet that records request id, shard id, model variant, latency_ms, upstream_status, and KV_cache_hit. The harness will upload a compressed CSV to the Drive link after the run.

Two asks from CloudCore:
1) Can you confirm whether you use client-side retries at the SDK layer? That will affect how we interpret 429 spikes.
2) Any regional egress constraints we should be aware of when routing to a failover region?

I'll be available to run the first set Mon–Tue, and can share the raw traces by Wednesday.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

Attachment referenced: redwood-test-plan-v1.xlsx (test harness + scripts)

From: Sanjay Shah <sanjay@cloudcore.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@cloudcore.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: reliability validation plan & next tests against CloudCore APIs

Thanks Tessa and Marcus — this looks good. A few answers and clarifications from our side: 

- We do have an SDK layer that retries idempotent requests with exponential backoff (max 3 retries). For the main evaluation we can disable client retries to get a clearer signal on Redwood behavior. We'll coordinate with our platform team to flip that.

- Regional constraints: our prod workloads are only allowed to egress from us-west-2 and europe-west1 for regulatory reasons. Routing to a third region is not allowed, but you can route to us-west-2 fallback.

- Availability window: we can open a short IP allow-listing window Tues 8/18 09:30–12:30 PT. That works for us.

Questions before we kick off: 
1) For the induced GPU OOM scenario, can you confirm whether the failover is automatic or requires a process restart? We want to know what counts as transparent failover vs manual intervention.
2) How will you surface error budgets and 429 trends in the post-run report? A per-minute time-series and an aggregated error budget burn rate would be ideal.

If those answers are quick we can lock Tuesday and aim to run the latency bakeoff in the morning.

Best,
Sanjay Shah
Platform Lead, CloudCore Inc.
sanjay@cloudcore.com

Date: 2026-08-18T09:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: reliability validation plan & next tests against CloudCore APIs

Perfect — thanks for the quick turnaround, Sanjay. Answers inline below and final logistics: 

1) Induced GPU OOM failover: Redwood's serving runtime will attempt automatic variant fallback for the affected request in-process (transparent to the caller) when it detects a runtime OOM during allocation. If node-level instability continues we have a node-replacement workflow that takes ~30–90s to bring a replacement, but by then most live requests should have been retried/fallbacked to the quantized variant. We'll instrument both: the per-request fallback flag + the node-replacement event time.

2) Error budget reporting: after the run we'll produce a short report (attached: latency-bakeoff-initial-results.pdf) with per-minute time-series for 5xx/4xx/429 rates, cumulative burn rate, and a table mapping incident windows to observed failover behavior. We'll also include a CSV of the raw trace (request id, timestamp, latency_ms, status, model_variant, kv_cache_hit).

Logistics confirmed:
- IP allow-listing window: Tue 8/18 09:30–12:30 PT (we'll use that for the primary runs)
- Marcus will execute the three scenarios starting at 09:40 PT and share the Drive link as soon as the CSV is uploaded
- Follow-up sync: Thurs 8/20 11:00 PT for a 45-min walkthrough of the results and decisioning on next steps (can be recorded)

If anything changes on your side please flag it in the HubSpot deal and drop a note here. Looking forward to the runs — we'll try to make the comparisons very transparent (latency profiles, retry semantics, and error-budget burn).

Thanks,

Tessa Morgan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
T: 415-555-0186 | tessa.morgan@redwood.com
